@@U01172@@
Our little 格蕾琴 pulls a long face, and thinks: “It’s a gift horse, after all; and how can the man nice enough to bring it, whoever he is, be bad?” So off her mother sends for one of those priests, and no sooner he understands the joke and likes what he sees, he says: “That's the spirit!” he says. “Who conquers his greed wins big. The church has a marvelous digestion: its gobbled up whole countries, and never been glutted. The church alone, dear ladies, can digest ill-gotten goods.”

@@U01174@@
Nothing new there; a king can do it the same as any Jew.

@@U01176@@
With that, he pockets the necklace, brooches, and rings as if they were so many mushrooms, thanking them neither more nor less than if he'd pocketed a bag of nuts. Promising them their reward in Heaven, he left then feeling edified.

@@U01178@@
And 格蕾琴?

@@U01180@@
She sits there restless, not knowing what to do or how, thinking day and night of the jewels, but even more about him who brought them.
translation:
@@U01172@@
我们的小格蕾琴板着脸，心想：“这毕竟是一匹礼物马，而送它来的人，不管他是谁，怎么可能是坏人呢？”于是，她的母亲派人去找一位牧师，他一听懂这个笑话并喜欢他所看到的，就说：“这就是精神！”他说。 “谁征服了自己的贪婪，谁就获得了巨大的胜利。教会有惊人的消化能力：它吞噬了整个国家，而且从未被过剩。亲爱的女士们，只有教会才能消化不义之财。”

@@U01174@@
那里没有什么新鲜事；国王可以像任何犹太人一样做到这一点。

@@U01176@@
说完，他把项链、胸针和戒指装进了口袋，就像它们是很多蘑菇一样，对它们的感谢就像他把一袋坚果装进口袋一样。他向他们许诺他们会在天堂得到奖赏，然后离开时感觉受到了启发。

@@U01178@@
还有格蕾琴？

@@U01180@@
她坐在那里坐立不安，不知道该做什么，也不知道该怎么做，日日夜夜地想着那些珠宝，但更多地想着那个带来它们的人。
